differences.evidence: The top half shows d followed by the separated short strokes of i/r and a final small a; the word is longer than dit and has no terminal t ascender.

differences.place: line 1 insertion and all later occurrences of the same capital
differences.evidence: C doubt retained. The inserted capital has two open, rounded lobes and no square vertical stem. This supports a calligraphic E representation, but the handwriting alone does not conclusively distinguish a script alphabet from a rounded ordinary E. The same form recurs throughout.
Two short quotation strokes occur before spéciale and again after it. There are no angular guillemet outlines.
The crop shows the comma after convenable and then the two cursive groups ou and ce, with no intervening punctuation.

C doubt resolved to the equals-like sign: two substantially straight horizontal strokes, with only an entry turn on the lower stroke and no repeated humps of m. H explicitly expands this sign in its editorial note. The written sign is retained.
The enlarged mark has a thick head and an unmistakable tapered tail slanting down to the left. It is a comma. Capital S in the following Si is preserved despite the comma.
C doubt resolved. The crop permits the sequence correspon-d-ent: an ascending d, followed by the extended e/n trace and the small terminal crossed t immediately before ainsi.

differences.place: line 8, cancelled capital before live G_n
differences.evidence: C doubt retained. A long descending stem curling left strongly supports cancelled G_n. Dense cancellation strokes occupy its upper body and leave a two-lobed E-like reading as a weaker supported possibility. A small n is visible to its right. No confident underlying correction sequence can be reconstructed.

differences.place: line 8, live G_n following the cancellation
differences.evidence: C doubt resolved to plain G. The detached roof-shaped trace occupies the position of the upper arc of the G; the lower portion lacks its own complete upper bowl. Thus the apparent roof supplies the broken upper loop rather than a separate accent above a complete letter.
C doubt resolved to de. After the looped d, the short horizontal exit and small terminal curl form e; there is no independent rounded u basin.
The new line En analogie has ordinary line spacing and starts at the same left text edge as the surrounding continuation lines. No blank line, indentation, or separator marks a paragraph break.

C doubt resolved. The crop shows the initial c/o loops, compressed paired m strokes, the u, the crossed t sequence and the n/t ending. Crowding is pen overlap within the word; no separate deletion can be read.

C doubt retained. A detached short lower-left stroke could be the lower barb of a left-pointing arrow, while the long shaft has a hooked right endpoint. The crop does not establish a complete left arrowhead. The next line has a clear right-pointing arrow, which makes inverse-limit notation plausible but does not itself decide this ink.

The crop shows the initial en, followed by a first g with a long descender, the intervening r/e/n/a strokes, and a second g descender before the final e. This is engrenage; mirage cannot account for the two g shapes or the beginning.

differences.final: small curved stroke, reproduced in TikZ and its position recorded
differences.evidence: A short pale curved stroke is visible below nous, separate from the word and the next line. Its linguistic or corrective function is undetermined. It is reproduced as a mark, without inventing a word or an insertion meaning.

differences.place: line 23, after familier and closing parenthesis
differences.evidence: The crop clearly shows three horizontal ellipsis strokes and a closing parenthesis. No distinct deliberate full stop is present between that parenthesis and Il; a tiny low pale speck does not have the weight or placement of the line’s written punctuation.

unresolved.place: line 1 inserted category capital, governing later occurrences
unresolved.reason: Rounded handwriting supports the calligraphic representation, but script versus ordinary E is not conclusively encoded by the glyph.

unresolved.place: line 8 cancelled capital before live G_n
unresolved.reason: Descending stem supports G; dense crossed upper strokes prevent excluding E or reconstructing a reliable overwriting sequence.
Lower-left short trace could be an arrow barb, but no complete head survives clearly in the crop.

notes.content: The page proposes calling an n-category spéciale or n-galoisienne when it is n-equivalent to the category of locally constant (n−1)-champs on a suitable space or topos, and proposes an equivalent description using n-functors from an n-groupoid to (n-Cat). It names the associated fundamental n-groupoid, local systems and geometric realization. By analogy with n=1 it then suggests recovering the groupoid as the full sub-n-category of underlined Hom_n consisting of functors having certain exactness properties. It mentions finite first-limit and arbitrary direct-limit preservation and the difficulty of n-limits. The final sentence remains incomplete at tout.

notes.page_date_title_evidence: Author number 25 at top centre; archival pencil 170 at bottom left. No date and no separate title occur on this sheet. The opening is a definition in continuous prose.
mathematics_triggered_reading_decisions: The contrast between finite first limits and arbitrary direct limits prompted a targeted crop of the weak first arrow, but the expected mathematical pairing was not used to remove the visible doubt.
The written rank n-systèmes was checked against the earlier (n−1)-champs; the differing ranks were preserved exactly. No change was inferred from H’s editorial reference to another language version.
The target notation has a tall C in the first (n-Cat), and short c in later (n-cat); capitalization was preserved without identifying the author’s convention.
The live symbol after the cancellation was read as G because the detached roof supplies its broken upper loop, not because a G is expected by the argument.
notes.mathematical_validation: No proof was attempted. The page contains proposed identifications and interpretations rather than a derivation. The rank, bracket and arrow inspections above are palaeographic/structural checks, not proofs of the mathematical assertions.
notes.nontext_mark: The isolated pale curved stroke below nous is recorded and drawn without assigning it a mathematical or linguistic function. Its authorship and purpose remain uncertain.
notes.emphasis_policy: Following the parent clarification, H’s emph is accepted as the same emphasis when its scope matches the manuscript single underline; no syntax-only emphasis differences are listed.
